- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.4) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4) in recent days, model underestimates; adjust upward to reflect bearish sentiment’s fading or reversal.
- Model consistently overpredicts prices in the 10–15 day horizon after recent spikes; apply downward correction for short-term momentum.
- Model underestimates prices in the 20+ day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; increase forecast slightly to account for mean reversion or delayed rally.
- If sentiment shows a sharp reversal (e.g., from -0.4 to +0.4 within 3 days), model often lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to capture sentiment shift.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment volatility in early horizon (1–5 days); add sentiment-weighted adjustment to first 5 days of forecast to reflect sentiment momentum.
